parts:
Hi Altuna,

I can confirm that tileMethylCounts() works with the example data that comes with your package (test1.myCpG.txt, test2.myCpG.txt, ...). Hence it seems to be an issue of my data or at least my data triggers something...

My Methylbase object 'meth' was generated from BSMAP/methratio output as follows( 6 samples in total; 2 conditions with 3 replicates each):

my_meth_obj=read(file.list,sample.id=as.list(sample_ids),treatment=my_treatment,assembly="mm10",header=TRUE, context="CpG", resolution="base",pipeline=list(fraction=TRUE,chr.col=1,start.col=2,end.col=2,strand.col=3,freqC.col=5,coverage.col=6 ))

# remove entries with zero coverage
for(i in 1:num_samples){
      print(paste("Removing NAs resulting from zero coverage from sample:",sample_ids[[i]],sep=" "))
      my_meth_obj[[i]]=my_meth_obj[[i]][!is.na(my_meth_obj[[i]]$numCs/my_meth_obj[[i]]$coverage),]
}


# Filtering
filtered.my_meth_obj=filterByCoverage(my_meth_obj,lo.count=7,lo.perc=NULL,hi.count=NULL,hi.perc=99.9)

#Merge samples
meth=unite(filtered.my_meth_obj,destrand=TRUE,min.per.group=3)

tiles=tileMethylCounts(meth,win.size=1000,step.size=1000)
Error: 'levels' is not an exported object from 'namespace:IRanges'

Any idea howto investigate this further? Unfortunately the original data set is too large for a reproducible example. Maybe I can break it down to a reasonable size for an example.

Best regards,
Michael

I can confirm that tileMethylCounts() in 0.9.4 in combination with BioC
3.0 now works as expected. Thanks for the quick fix!

Best regards,
Michael

On 10/28/14 21:21, Altuna Akalin wrote:
> Hi,
> I pushed 0.9.4 on github, now tileMethylCounts on methylBase objects works
> again, let me know if it doesn't.
> https://github.com/al2na/methylKit#installation
>
> Best,
> Altuna
>
> On Sun, Oct 26, 2014 at 6:54 AM, Jason liao <liaoj...@gmail.com
> <mailto:liaoj...@gmail.com>> wrote:
>
> Hi, Altuna, I've encounter similar issue. Good to know you have identified
> the issue. Thanks for all the help.
>
> Best,
>
> Jason

> 在 2014年10月25日星期六UTC+8上午1时13分16秒，Altuna Akalin写道：

> Ok. I just realized that this is probably an issue with the version of
> the function that is specific to methlyBase objects. I will try to fix
> it next week.
>
> Best
> Altuna

> On Friday, October 24, 2014, Altuna Akalin <aak...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > It would be great if you can subset the data for a minimal example. I will try to look into it as well, but if I can't reproduce the error, it would be difficult/impossible to fix it.
> >
> > Best
> > Altuna
> >
> > On Friday, October 24, 2014, <becks...@zbh.uni-hamburg.de__> wrote:
> >> Hi Altuna,
> >> I can confirm that tileMethylCounts() works with the example data
> that comes with your package (test1.myCpG.txt, test2.myCpG.txt, ...).
> Hence it seems to be an issue of my data or at least my data triggers
> something...
> >> My Methylbase object 'meth' was generated from BSMAP/methratio
> output as follows( 6 samples in total; 2 conditions with 3 replicates each):

> >> my_meth_obj=read(file.list,sam__ple.id
> <http://sample.id>=as.list(sample_ids),__treatment=my_treatment,__assembly="mm10",header=TRUE,
> context="CpG",
> resolution="base",pipeline=__list(fraction=TRUE,chr.col=1,__start.col=2,end.col=2,strand.__col=3,freqC.col=5,coverage.__col=6

> ))
> >> # remove entries with zero coverage
> >> for(i in 1:num_samples){
> >> print(paste("Removing NAs resulting from zero coverage from
> sample:",sample_ids[[i]],sep=" "))

> >> my_meth_obj[[i]]=my_meth_obj[[__i]][!is.na
> <http://is.na>(my_meth_obj[[i]]$__numCs/my_meth_obj[[i]]$__coverage),]
> >> }
> >>
> >> # Filtering
> >>
> filtered.my_meth_obj=__filterByCoverage(my_meth_obj,__lo.count=7,lo.perc=NULL,hi.__count=NULL,hi.perc=99.9)
> >> #Merge samples
> >> meth=unite(filtered.my_meth___obj,destrand=TRUE,min.per.__group=3)
> >>
> >> tiles=tileMethylCounts(meth,__win.size=1000,step.size=1000)

> >> Error: 'levels' is not an exported object from 'namespace:IRanges'
> >>
> >>
> >>
> >> Any idea howto investigate this further? Unfortunately the original
> data set is too large for a reproducible example. Maybe I can break it
> down to a reasonable size for an example.
> >> Best regards,
> >> Michael
> >>
> >>
> >>
